correctness.rationale: Partial fractions give the difference of signed exponential Fourier transforms divided by b²−a². Poisson summation with the same positive Zak phase gives the common phase exp(i theta xi) and the difference of the two stated hyperbolic kernels. Taking the divided difference as b→a gives the stated i pi²/a prefactor times the lambda derivative. Away from sin(theta)=0 and xi=1/2, a zero requires simultaneous cancellation of both real coefficients. Their ratio has nonvanishing derivative of sign 1−2xi, excluding both equality at distinct poles and simultaneous derivative cancellation at a repeated pole. At xi=1/2 the common coefficient cosh(lambda/2)/(cosh(lambda)−cos(theta)) decreases with strictly negative derivative. On theta=0 and pi the respective sinh and cosh ratios have strictly signed lambda derivatives except at the stated interior zero, by strict increase of s coth(lambda s) and s tanh(lambda s). At xi=0 the kernel is 1+i sin(theta)/(cosh(lambda)−cos(theta)); cancellation leaves zeros exactly at theta=0 and pi. The defining series is C¹ in both variables by summable bounds on g', k g and g, so boundary derivatives can be taken from the interior. At (theta,xi)=(0,0),(pi,0),(0,1/2) respectively, the theta derivatives of the kernel are i/(cosh(lambda)−1), −i/(cosh(lambda)+1), and i cosh(lambda/2)/(cosh(lambda)−1); the xi derivatives are −lambda coth(lambda/2), −lambda tanh(lambda/2), and −lambda/sinh(lambda/2). Every displayed scalar factor has strictly signed derivative: for the last factors this follows from sinh x cosh x>x, positivity of tanh x+x sech² x, and x cosh x>sinh x, respectively. Taking differences or lambda derivatives therefore leaves two nonzero perpendicular derivatives at every zero. The nonzero common complex prefactor and theta=2 pi t preserve nonsingularity. The proof covers all positive parameters; the reported grid and numerical Jacobian checks are only corroborative and the frozen script was not executed.

evidence: For g_1, Proposition 2.1 restricts unit-circle roots to z=±1 on the first half of the frequency cell; Proposition 2.3 and Remark 2.2 transfer root constraints to the Zak transform, and reality gives the other frequency half. Evaluating Q at z=±1 reduces to differences of the two scalar sinh/cosh ratios at lambda=2 pi and 4 pi, so the (1,2) classification is a short consequence of the prior representation and restriction. A sentence following Theorem 3.1 suggests vanishing at every z for xi=1/2, but Remark 2.1 actually gives reciprocity or anti-reciprocity, not that identity. At z=−1 and xi=1/2 the difference of 1/cosh(pi) and 1/cosh(2 pi) is nonzero in the same representation.
The ray comparator supplies derivative information at (0,0) and (1/2,0), but not every simplicity test or a complete arbitrary-ratio classification.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Do not count the fixed-pair two-fiber restriction or the forced zeros as new. Extending a fixed unit-period window to an arbitrary pole ratio cannot be done by scale substitution, which preserves the pole ratio and changes the period. Coalescence and transversality also do not follow from a distinct-pole count by continuity. The uniform strict derivative and ratio arguments establish the surviving claim.

value.rationale: For odd windows symmetry alone leaves open both extra zeros and tangential zeros. Resolving both questions for a natural two-pole family, including the repeated-pole degeneration, gives a useful exact invariant for analyses involving Zak zeros and local stability. Its relevance does not depend on claiming a complete Gabor frame-set theorem, which the result does not give.
